New criminal laws BNS, BNSS and BSA in force, with mandatory forensic examination for grave offences and technology-driven investigation — capacity, not statute, is the binding constraint.

Indian Carbon Market Portal launched 21 Mar 2026. Iron & steel and fertiliser targets still pending. SWM Rules 2026 Notified Jan 2026, in force 1 April 2026; supersede SWM Rules 2016. Four streams — wet, dry, sanitary, special-care. EBWGR for generators ≥100 kg/day, ≥40,000 l/day water, or ≥20,000 sq m. EU CBAM Definitive phase began 1 January 2026 — certificate purchase, not just reporting. BBNJ Entered into force January 2026; 3rd implementing agreement under UNCLOS; four pillars — marine genetic resources, area-based management tools, EIA, capacity building. CCUS ₹20,000 crore over 5 years (Budget 2026-27). Mangroves 5,000 sq km in India ( 3% of global cover); Sundarbans alone >40% of the Indian total. Ramsar sites 80+ in India — the largest number in South Asia. Wetlands rule Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 — notification left to States. Disaster management DM (Amendment) Act 2025 Act No. 10 of 2025. Urban Disaster Management Authorities in State capitals and municipal-corporation cities (Delhi, Chandigarh excluded); National Disaster Database; statutory status for the High Level Committee approving NDRF/NDMF assistance. Only Karnataka had constituted a UDMA as of the government’s own release. Mission Mausam Launched 2025; IMD AI/ML models give up to seven-day advance prediction incl. flood forecasting and cyclone tracking. First Heat Action Plan Ahmedabad, 2013 — first in South Asia. 1999 Odisha super-cyclone 10,000+ deaths, against single or double-digit mortality in recent landfalls. 16th FC disaster allocation ₹1.55 lakh crore; 90:10 sharing for NE and Himalayan States, 75:25 for others. Internal security CII Defined under Section 70, IT Act 2000; NCIIPC is the nodal agency. CERT-In 2022 directions Incident reporting within 6 hours; log retention mandated. Cybercrime helpline 1930 — National Cybercrime Reporting Portal / I4C. UN Convention against Cybercrime Opened for signature at Hanoi, October 2025 — first global cybercrime treaty; India is not a Budapest Convention party. Terror finance law UAPA 1967 Chapter IV-A; PMLA 2002 (ED); NIA for scheduled offences; FIU-IND for STRs. India is in the FATF regular follow-up category. Theatre commands 17 existing single-service commands, proposed for consolidation. CDS and Department of Military Affairs created 2019. Maritime IMAC at Gurugram; IFC-IOR hosts partner-navy liaison officers. NC3I network links coastal radar and AIS. LWE Affected-district count has fallen steeply; FRA 2006 and PESA 1996 are the consolidation instruments.

Algorithmic decisions Four design duties where the State uses an algorithm to affect a right: notice that the decision is automated; reasons in the person's language; audit of logs, bias and impact; and a human appeal with a statutory clock — grounded in Art 14 arbitrariness, Art 21 fair procedure and Puttaswamy proportionality.
Probity in data Purpose limitation, security, minimisation and non-discrimination bind every large State data exercise; the Census Act, 1948 makes enumeration data confidential and non-justiciable.
Whistle-blower protection The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 remains substantially unoperationalised — the standing gap between a duty to disclose and a system that protects the discloser.

sections.h: The Exemplar Bank, And The Thinkers

items.d: The three commonest directives in GS-4 since 2013 are illustrate, substantiate and justify — all three demand instances, so a point without an example is half a point.
Named Indian officers and citizens outrank invented ones and outrank foreign ones.

Each entry below is written to be droppable into a sentence: the person, the one specific act, and the value it demonstrates. Never fabricate: an examiner has been recorded writing a bare ‘??’ against an unverifiable claim.

groups.g: Civil servants — the act, then the value

items.d: T. N. Seshan As Chief Election Commissioner, enforced the Model Code and expenditure limits using powers the office had always held. Institutional capacity is often latent rather than absent — use for institutional integrity, for courage within authority, and against the claim that reform needs new law.

Satyendra Dubey NHAI engineer; a specific, documented complaint on the Golden Quadrilateral through the proper channel, with a request for anonymity that was not honoured; murdered in 2003. Courage exercised correctly and unprotected — the standing argument for notifying the Whistle Blowers Protection Act.

Ashok Khemka Recorded dissent through channels across a large number of transfers. The sustainable form of moral courage — the note that survives the officer — and the standing case for a Civil Services Board and minimum tenure.

S. R. Sankaran Sought postings where bonded labour and Dalit deprivation were densest; releases followed from the presence, not from the circular. Empathy as a method rather than a sentiment; also for objectivity joined to compassion.

Armstrong Pame Sub-divisional officer in Manipur; built a hundredkilometre road by crowd-funding when sanction would not come. Initiative within the law where the system is slow — use for dedication to duty and for emotional intelligence as persuasion.
U. Sagayam Tamil Nadu officer; asset declarations published voluntarily and repeated action against illegal quarrying. Transparency exercised beyond obligation.
Kiran Bedi Tihar reforms — education, meditation, grievance boxes and open petitioning inside the prison. Reform of an institution by changing what happens daily rather than by amending the manual.

E. Sreedharan Delhi Metro; publicly owned the 2009 Zamrudpur girder collapse and offered to resign. Accountability for outcome by the person who benefited from success; also technical competence joined to public ownership of failure.

Vinod Rai As CAG, audits establishing that procedural compliance and probity are separate tests. Use for the below-threshold contract split, for propriety audit, and for the limits of a rule-based defence.
Lal Bahadur Shastri Resigned as Railway Minister after the 1956 Ariyalur accident, establishing a convention no rule required. Self-imposed accountability; also for ‘he who cannot rule himself’.
Sardar Patel Defended a permanent, impartial service in the Constituent Assembly — the ‘steel frame’ speech. Use for non-partisanship and for the constitutional choice to retain the service.

Ira Singhal Topped the civil services examination after an earlier allotment was denied despite rank on grounds of disability. Prejudice operating through a neutral-sounding criterion of ‘suitability’; also for reasonable accommodation.

Aruna Roy and MKSS The jan sunwai in Rajasthan — public reading of muster rolls and bills before the assembly of those they describe — which produced both the social audit method and the RTI movement. Use for transparency, for social audit, and as the proof that authority-redistributing reform needs a constituency outside the administration.
Ela Bhatt SEWA — organising self-employed women and building trust-based lending where collateral was impossible. Dignity of labour and institutionbuilding from below.
Dashrath Manjhi Twenty-two years cutting a road through a hill in Gehlaur after his wife died for want of one. Perseverance and a value learnt from loss; use sparingly and never as mere inspiration.

Gandhi Public confession of his own failings as an instrument of authority; the talisman; means and ends as convertible terms. Use for self-examination, for trusteeship, and for the test of a decision’s effect on the last person.

Ambedkar Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for water access; the Constituent Assembly warning of a life of contradictions; constitutional morality as cultivated rather than natural. Use for fraternity, for law preceding social consent, and for democracy as associated living. The Banyan, Chennai Community-based recovery care integrated within residential areas. Use for stigma, siting decisions and community living under the Mental Healthcare Act. Odisha’s cyclone record Phailin and after — evacuation of over a million with very low casualties, on a practised drill, a shelter network built in advance and last-mile warning. Use for preparedness, for emotional intelligence in crisis command, and for the point that response capability is not risk reduction. Failure cases worth naming Aadhaar authentication failures concentrated among manual workers and the aged, and reported starvation deaths in Jharkhand · manual scavenging surviving the 2013 prohibition, largely through sanitation contracts · the 2022 AIIMS Delhi ransomware attack, attributed in Parliament to improper network segmentation (the deferred patch case is NHS WannaCry 2017, not AIIMS) · the Kumbakonam school fire (2004) · Bhagalpur (1989) as the cost of deferring to the loudest party · Erwadi · Satyam (2009) as a board and audit failure. Western thinkers — the concept and its administrative use Aristotle Virtue by habituation; the mean between excess and deficiency; phronesis, practical wisdom as judgment of particulars. Use for moral courage, discretion, and why training cannot produce character. Kant The categorical imperative; universalisability; the formula of humanity — never treat a person merely as a means. Use for consent, data, workers and any efficiency purchased at someone’s expense. Bentham & Mill Greatest happiness; Mill’s harm principle — dislike is not injury — and the publicity principle. Use for aggregation, public order, siting and paternalism. Rawls Original position, veil of ignorance, difference principle, lexical priority of liberty; Law of Peoples on duties of assistance. Use for displacement, targeting, reservation and foreign funding. Nozick Entitlement theory — a distribution is just if it arose justly. The honest counter to Rawls. Amartya Sen Capability rather than resources; entitlement failure — deprivation from collapse of access, not absence of supply; comparative rather than transcendental justice. Use for exclusion, relief and the critique of Rawls. Max Weber Ethic of responsibility against ethic of conviction; the official’s honour in executing an order as if it were his own conviction; legal-rational authority. Use for decisions under uncertainty and for neutrality. Adam Smith The impartial spectator — the internalised observer whose judgment is neither one’s own interest nor the crowd’s. Use for objectivity with empathy. Lon Fuller / H. L. A. Hart The inner morality of law — eight conditions of legality — against the separation of law and morals. Use for the rule of law and conscience question. Martin Luther King Jr Letter from Birmingham Jail on the unjust law that degrades human personality; Stride Toward Freedom on law restraining the heartless. Kohlberg Pre-conventional, conventional, post-conventional moral development. Use for value formation, and to distinguish a code of conduct from a code of ethics. Gordon Allport The Nature of Prejudice (1954); the contact hypothesis — equal-status, cooperative, sanctioned contact reduces prejudice. Festinger Cognitive dissonance — behaviour change can precede attitude change; also the engine of rationalisation in ethical fading. Bandura Social learning — values acquired by modelling and vicarious reinforcement rather than instruction. Milgram · Asch · Zimbardo Obedience to authority · conformity to a visibly wrong majority · situational production of cruelty. The three experiments that explain administrative complicity without invoking individual vice. Hirschman Exit, voice and loyalty — voice before exit; and the citizen who cannot exit needs an effective voice. Use for whistleblowing and for citizen’s charters. Klitgaard Corruption = monopoly + discretion – accountability. Converts exhortation into a design brief. Bazerman & Tenbrunsel Ethical fading and bounded ethicality; with Vaughan’s normalisation of deviance, the pair for the slow slide. James Reason Just culture and the substitution test — would a similarly trained officer plausibly have done the same? Use to separate error, negligence and misconduct. Goleman · Salovey & Mayer Five competencies (self-awareness, selfregulation, motivation, empathy, social skill) against the four-branch ability model. Use for emotional intelligence. Maslach · Hochschild Burnout triad — exhaustion, depersonalisation, reduced accomplishment — and emotional labour. Use for empathy fatigue. Edmondson Psychological safety — whether bad news travels upward in time to act on. Converts EI into an organisational property. Schein Artefacts, espoused values, basic assumptions — the three levels of organisational culture, of which the third governs.
Freeman / Friedman Stakeholder theory against the shareholder view. Use for corporate governance and for private-sector dilemmas.
Nolan Seven principles of public life — selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, openness, honesty, leadership (1995). The one Western code the paper expects by name.
Finer / Friedrich External enforceable control against inner professional responsibility. The standard pairing for accountability questions.
Thaler & Sunstein Libertarian paternalism; the nudge, whose own test is that it must be cheap to avoid.
Ambedkar ‘Democracy is not merely a form of Government. It is primarily a mode of associated living.’ Form is not substance; democracy lives where people meet as equals.
Ambedkar ‘Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated.’ The forms are a top-dressing on an undemocratic soil.
Ambedkar ‘However good a Constitution may be, if those who are implementing it are not good, it will prove to be bad.’ Institutions are only as good as the discretion exercised inside them.
Ambedkar ‘Political democracy cannot last unless there lies at the base of it social democracy.’ Equality at the ballot cannot survive inequality at the well.
Ambedkar ‘I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved.’ The condition of the least-powered group is the index of the whole.
Rawls ‘Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought.’ A priority, not a preference: injustice disqualifies an institution however efficient.

Rawls ‘Each person possesses an inviolability founded on justice that even the welfare of society as a whole cannot override.’ Rights are not to be traded against aggregate gain — the answer to any displacement or targeting question.
Mandela ‘A nation should not be judged by how it treats its highest citizens, but its lowest ones.’ The measure is the citizen least able to complain.
Mandela ‘Poverty is not natural. It is man-made and it can be overcome and eradicated by the actions of human beings.’ Deprivation is an administrative outcome, not a background condition.
Martin Luther King Jr ‘Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.’ A tolerated exception becomes the precedent for the next one.
Amartya Sen ‘Development can be seen as a process of expanding the real freedoms that people enjoy.’ Measure capability, not disbursement.
Nehru ‘The service of India means the service of the millions who suffer… the ending of poverty and ignorance and disease and inequality of opportunity.’ Public service defined by whom it is owed to.
Cicero ‘Salus populi suprema lex esto’ — let the welfare of the people be the highest law. The purpose of the rule outranks its letter.
Lord Acton ‘Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.’ Corruption is a function of the position, not of the character brought to it.
Madison ‘If men were angels, no government would be necessary.’ Design institutions for the officer you will actually get.
Madison ‘Ambition must be made to counteract ambition.’ Separation of functions rather than exhortation.

Kautilya ‘Just as it is impossible not to taste honey placed on the tongue, so it is impossible for one dealing with government funds not to taste at least a little of the King’s wealth.’ The classic Indian case for audit and supervision rather than trust — the single best quotation for a probity answer.
Kautilya ‘In the happiness of his subjects lies the king’s happiness; in their welfare, his welfare.’ Yogakshema as the declared object of the State.
Jefferson ‘When a man assumes a public trust, he should consider himself as public property.’ The fiduciary conception of office.
Bentham ‘The more strictly we are watched, the better we behave.’ The publicity principle — use for RTI and s. 4 disclosure.
Brandeis ‘Sunlight is said to be the best of disinfectants; electric light the most efficient policeman.’ Transparency as a preventive rather than punitive instrument.

Lord Hewart, R v Sussex Justices (1924) ‘Justice should not only be done, but should manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done.’ The whole argument for recusal, published criteria and reasoned orders.
Weber The official’s honour lies in executing an order as if it corresponded to his own conviction. Neutrality as a demanding moral position, not the absence of one.

Gandhi ‘Power based on love is a thousand times more effective and permanent than the one derived from fear of punishment.’ Consent outlasts coercion — for police–public relations and community policing. Goodhart / Strathern ‘When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.’ Every appraisal grading, utilisation certificate and disposal statistic. Quotations · integrity, truth and conscience Gandhi ‘The means may be likened to a seed, the end to a tree.’ Ends do not sanctify means; they are grown from them. Gandhi ‘Truth never damages a cause that is just.’ The disclosure that is feared is usually the one that is owed. Gandhi ‘There is a higher court than courts of justice and that is the court of conscience.’ Use only with the discipline that conscience operates through the record. Kant ‘Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.’ Test the rule you are relying on by making it general. Kant ‘Act so that you treat humanity… never merely as a means to an end, but always at the same time as an end.’ The formula of humanity — for consent, data, workers, and efficiency bought at someone’s expense. Confucius ‘The superior man understands what is right; the inferior man understands what will sell.’ The distinction between propriety and advantage. Marcus Aurelius ‘Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.’ Against the preachy register the examiner penalises. Socrates ‘The unexamined life is not worth living.’ Unexamined values are held conventionally and collapse when contradicted. Bhagavad Gita 2.47 ‘Your right is to work only, never to its fruits.’ Nishkama karma — duty discharged without regard to personal return; for dedication to duty. Bhagavad Gita 3.21 ‘Whatever a great man does, others follow; whatever standard he sets, the world pursues.’ Leadership by example — for ‘he who cannot rule himself’ and for work culture. Thiruvalluvar ‘It is compassion, the most gracious of virtues, which moves the world.’ Aram as the ground of both wealth and pleasure. Vivekananda ‘They alone live who live for others.’ Service as the content of a life rather than its decoration. Quotations · compassion, service and the last person

Gandhi’s talisman ‘Recall the face of the poorest and weakest man you have seen, and ask yourself if the step you contemplate is going to be of any use to him.’ The operational test for any administrative decision — the single most usable quotation in the paper.

Vivekananda ‘So long as millions live in hunger and ignorance, I hold every man a traitor who, having been educated at their expense, pays not the least heed to them.’ The debt a publicly educated officer owes.
Tagore ‘I slept and dreamt that life was joy. I awoke and saw that life was service. I acted and behold, service was joy.’ Service as vocation rather than sacrifice.
Buddha ‘Hatred does not cease by hatred, but only by love; this is the eternal rule.’ For communal situations and for de-escalation.
Mother Teresa ‘Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love.’ For the frontline tier, where quality is actually produced.
Ambedkar ‘Cultivation of mind should be the ultimate aim of human existence.’ For education and capacity building.
Martin Luther King Jr ‘Our lives begin to end the day we become silent about things that matter.’ Silence as a decision, not an omission.
Martin Luther King Jr ‘The ultimate measure of a man is not where he stands in moments of comfort and convenience, but where he stands at times of challenge and controversy.’ Courage tested by cost.
Martin Luther King Jr ‘One has a moral responsibility to disobey unjust laws.’ — Letter from Birmingham Jail. Pair always with his own test: openly, lovingly, and accepting the penalty.
Gandhi ‘In matters of conscience, the law of majority has no place.’ Prejudice is entitled to be heard and answered, not to decide.
Vivekananda ‘Strength is life, weakness is death.’ Capability as the precondition of virtue.
Tagore ‘Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high…’ Administration should release rather than discipline the citizen.
Thucydides (Pericles) ‘The secret of happiness is freedom, and the secret of freedom is courage.’ For moral courage and for whistleblowing.
Sardar Patel ‘Every Indian should now forget that he is a Rajput, a Sikh or a Jat… he must remember that he is an Indian.’ For non-partisanship and for fraternity.

Unattributed (set in UPSC 2020) ‘He who is unable to rule over himself can never really succeed in ruling over others.’ Authority over others is derivative of authority over oneself. Reproduce it without an attribution — the common ascriptions to Plato and to Confucius are both unverified.
Heraclitus ‘Character is destiny.’ Use only if you then show what built the character — otherwise it is decoration.

Aristotle No single line does the work — the usable Aristotle is the doctrine: virtue is acquired by habituation rather than instruction, and courage is the mean between cowardice and rashness. State the doctrine and attribute it; do not hunt for a quotable sentence.
Socrates ‘I know that I know nothing.’ Intellectual humility as the condition of learning — for after-action review and social audit.
Vivekananda ‘Education is the manifestation of the perfection already in man.’ Training draws out rather than installs.
Mandela ‘Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.’
Tagore ‘Don’t limit a child to your own learning, for he was born in another time.’ For NEP-type questions and for intergenerational value transmission.
Gandhi ‘Swaraj is to be attained by educating the masses to a sense of their capacity to regulate and control authority.’ Self-rule before self-government.
Martin Luther King Jr ‘The law may not change the heart, but it can restrain the heartless.’ Law reaches conduct, not belief — and for the victim, conduct is what matters.
Ambedkar ‘Law and order are the medicine of the body politic, and when the body politic gets sick, medicine must be administered.’ Enforcement as a duty rather than an option.

Lon Fuller The inner morality of law — generality, publicity, prospectivity, clarity, non-contradiction, possibility, constancy, congruence. Eight tests a rule must pass before it is even eligible for obedience.
Justinian / classical maxim ‘Fiat justitia ruat caelum’ — let justice be done though the heavens fall. Use as the position you then qualify, since administration must also weigh consequence.
Woodrow Wilson ‘It is getting to be harder to run a constitution than to frame one.’ Implementation, not design, is where governance fails.
Peter Drucker ‘There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all.’ For the abolition of an unnecessary requirement — the Socratic administrative duty.
Commonly misattributed — use with care or not at all

‘Be the change you wish to see in the world’ Not found in Gandhi’s writings. The closest authentic text is: ‘If we could change ourselves, the tendencies in the world would also change.’ Quote the second, or drop it.

‘We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act but a habit’ Will Durant, summarising Aristotle in The Story of Philosophy — not Aristotle’s words. Attribute the doctrine of habituation to Aristotle instead.
‘The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing’ No such sentence has been found in Burke. Use King’s ‘our lives begin to end the day we become silent’ instead.
‘The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice’ Theodore Parker (1853), popularised by King. Safe if you say ‘in the phrase King made famous’.
‘Integrity is doing the right thing when no one is watching’ Widely given to C. S. Lewis; unverified. State the proposition in your own words.
‘First they came…’ Martin Niemöller — correctly attributed but very often garbled; reproduce only if you are sure of the wording.

The general rule In this paper your examples are your content, so a fabricated or misattributed one costs more than an omission — an examiner has been recorded writing a bare ‘??’ against an unverifiable claim. If unsure of the wording, paraphrase the idea and name the thinker without quotation marks.

sections.h: The Code Bank And The Vocabulary

items.d: The code layer — the report, the statute, the rule, the section — is the one most can- didates skip and the one that most reliably separates copies. It costs six words and converts an opinion into an anchored claim. Verify anything you intend to quote: in this paper a confidently wrong citation costs more than a cautious omission. Reports and commissions Second ARC (2005–09, Veerappa Moily) The paper’s single most useful anchor. 4th Report Ethics in Governance — a Code of Ethics distinct from the conduct rules, a Public Services Bill, time limits in disciplinary proceedings, confiscation of illegally acquired property, disqualification on framing of charge for serious offences. 12th Report Citizen Centric Administration — the seven-step Sevottam model, and the insistence that a charter carry a remedy. Also 1st Right to Information, 5th Public Order, 7th Conflict Resolution, 10th Personnel Administration, 11th e-Governance. First ARC (1966–70) Recommended the Lokpal and Lokayukta; the desk officer system; separation of accounts from audit. Nolan Committee (UK, 1995) Seven principles of public life. The model for a code of ethics as against a code of conduct. Santhanam Committee (1962) Led to the Central Vigilance Commission (1964). Vohra Committee (1993) The criminal–political–bureaucratic nexus. Kotak Committee (2017) Listed-company governance — independent directors, board composition, disclosure. Isher Ahluwalia (2011) Urban infrastructure and services, for municipal service-quality questions. International Paris Principles (1993) for national human rights institutions · OECD Principles of Corporate Governance · UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights · FATF standards on non-profit sector risk. Statutes, rules and sections to cite Conduct and service AIS (Conduct) Rules 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules 1964 — Rule 3: absolute integrity, devotion to duty, nothing unbecoming; Rule 3(3)(iii) — oral directions to be confirmed in writing, the single most citable rule in this paper. Bar on political activity, private trade, gifts, speculation and unauthorised communication with the press; annual immovable property return. CCS (CCA) Rules 1965 and AIS (D&A) Rules 1969 for procedure; FR 56(j) for compulsory retirement in the public interest; Article 311 for the safeguards and the three exceptions. Integrity and anti-corruption Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, amended 2018 — bribe-giving made an offence, corporate liability, criminal misconduct narrowed to illicit enrichment and misappropriation, and s. 17A prior approval before any inquiry into an official decision. Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 (Lokpal constituted 2019) and its asset declaration requirement. CVC Act 2003. Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 — gazetted 12 May 2014 and never brought into force, which is the standing gap in every courage and disclosure answer. PMLA 2002; Benami Amendment 2016; Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018. Transparency RTI Act 2005 — s. 4 suo motu disclosure (the least used and most important), s. 7 timelines (30 days; 48 hours for life and liberty), s. 8 exemptions with the s. 8(2) public interest override, s. 10 severability, s. 20 penalty up to ₹25,000. The 2019 amendment moved Commissioners’ tenure and conditions from statute to rules; the DPDP Act 2023 amended s. 8(1)(j), removing the qualifying test and widening the personalinformation exemption — its s. 44(3) came into force on 13 Nov 2025. Data and technology DPDP Act 2023 — notice, consent, purpose limitation, data minimisation, breach notification, and wide State exemptions. Aadhaar Act 2016 s. 7 — note the proviso covers the person to whom a number is not assigned, not one whose authentication fails. The ‘authentication failure cannot extinguish an entitlement’ proposition rests on Reg. 12, Aadhaar (Authentication) Regulations 2016, UIDAI/MeitY exceptionhandling circulars, and Puttaswamy (II), the Aadhaar judgment of 26 Sept 2018 — not the 2017 privacy judgment. CERT-In directions 2022 — six-hour incident reporting. IT Rules 2021 on intermediary due diligence and platform accountability; CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023 for deceptive design. Service delivery and rights Sevottam / IS 15700; State public services guarantee Acts — Madhya Pradesh 2010, Bihar, Rajasthan, Karnataka’s Sakala — notified services, timelines, designated officer, appeal, personal penalty. CPGRAMS and the Directorate of Public Grievances. VB–G RAM G Act 2025 — the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, assented 21 Dec 2025 and in force 1 July 2026, which by s. 37 repeals MGNREGA 2005: s. 5 guarantee of 125 days, s. 11 unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days, s. 20 social audit of works by the Gram Sabha, ss. 23–24 transparency and weekly digital disclosure, s. 27 penalty for contravention up to ₹10,000. Cite the new Act by name; MGNREGA is now repealed law. NFSA 2013; RTI; RTE 2009; Forest Rights Act 2006 s. 4(5) — no eviction while claims are pending; RFCTLARR Act 2013 — SIA, consent, Second Schedule. Dignity and non-discrimination Mental Healthcare Act 2017 — s. 19 right to community living, s. 20 protection from cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment, s. 21 equality and non-discrimination. RPwD Act 2016 — reasonable accommodation. POSH Act 2013 and the Vishaka guidelines that preceded it. Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013. Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955; SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989. PC & PNDT Act 1994.

Corporate and platform Companies Act 2013 — s. 134(3) board responsibility and material disclosure, s. 135 CSR, s. 177 audit committee and s. 177(9) vigil mechanism, s. 188 related-party transactions. SEBI LODR; NFRA; Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting. Code on Social Security 2020 — s. 113 registration of gig and platform workers, s. 114 schemes for them, s. 141 the Social Security Fund.

Financial propriety GFR 2017 — the bar on splitting a purchase to avoid a sanction requirement, the single most usable citation for the contractsplitting case; Delegation of Financial Powers Rules 1978; CVC guidance on tender thresholds and on third-party quality audit; CAG’s (DPC) Act 1971.

Safety, disaster and public order National Building Code and IS 456 coretesting provisions. Disaster Management Act 2005 ss. 25, 30 and 65; NDMA relief norms and SDRF scales; the 2025 amendment — statutory crisis management committees, plans prepared by NDMA/SDMA, a national disaster database, Urban Disaster Management Authorities. BNSS ss. 163 and 168 (formerly CrPC 144 and 149); BNSS s. 218 sanction for prosecution. New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019 on accelerated approval with postmarketing obligations.

Constitutional provisions Preamble — justice, liberty, equality, fraternity with the dignity of the individual. Art 14 — reasoned, non-arbitrary action (E. P. Royappa). Art 15, 17, 46. Art 19(1)(a),(b),(c) with 19(2)–(4). Art 21 — dignity, fair procedure (Maneka Gandhi), privacy and proportionality (Puttaswamy). Art 25. Art 51A Fundamental Duties, including 51A(k) on parental duty. Arts 32, 148, 226, 311.

Training and capacity Mission Karmayogi (2020) — the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building; the Capacity Building Commission; iGOT; the FRAC architecture and the three competency families — behavioural, functional, domain. National Training Policy 2012. LBSNAA’s village attachment and Bharat Darshan. NEP 2020 on ethics and constitutional values.

Puttaswamy (2017) Informational privacy as a facet of Article 21; the majority’s three-fold test — legality, legitimate aim, proportionality. The structured four-stage test is from Puttaswamy (II), the 2018 Aadhaar judgment.
Maneka Gandhi (1978) Procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.
E. P. Royappa (1974) Arbitrariness is itself a denial of equality.
Vishaka (1997) Judicially framed guidelines in a legislative vacuum, later the POSH Act 2013.
M. C. Mehta v Kamal Nath (1997) The public trust doctrine received into Indian law.
Vellore Citizens’ Welfare Forum (1996) The precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle.
Noel Harper (2022) FCRA ss. 7, 12(1A) and 17(1) upheld — the designated SBI New Delhi account and the bar on sub-granting; s. 12A read down to allow an Indian passport in lieu of Aadhaar.
Vineet Narain (1997) Insulation of investigation; the CVC’s supervisory role.
Prakash Singh (2006) Seven police-reform directions, formally complied with and substantively evaded — the standard illustration of decoupling.
T. S. R. Subramanian (2013) Civil Services Board and minimum tenure; oral instructions to be recorded.
Dev Dutt (2008) Every appraisal entry must be communicated to the officer.
Phronesis Aristotle — practical wisdom; the judgment of particulars that no rule supplies.
Moral perception Seeing that a routine decision carries an irreversible human consequence.
Answerability The willingness to record reasons and be judged by them rather than by the outcome alone.
Ethical competence The capacity to judge whether an action ought to be performed, as against the capacity to perform it.
Ethical dissonance The discomfort of acting against one’s own standard — resolved either by changing the act or by revising the standard.
Ethical fading Bazerman and Tenbrunsel — the process by which the ethical content of a decision ceases to be perceived at all.
Normalisation of deviance Vaughan — a repeated small departure becomes the standard against which the next is judged.
Bounded ethicality The systematic ways in which people act against their own ethical standards without noticing.
Moral licensing Past good conduct treated as a credit against present lapse.

Conflict of interest Not a finding of influence but of reasonable doubt about it — hence disclosure and recusal, not protestation. Recusal Withdrawal from a decision in which one has an interest; not abdication but what allows the decision to be believed. Whistleblowing Disclosure of wrongdoing by an insider; internal and on the record before external, in Hirschman’s sequence. Substitution test Reason — would a similarly trained officer, similarly placed, plausibly have done the same? If yes, the finding belongs to the system. Just culture An accountability regime that distinguishes error, negligence and misconduct and responds differently to each. Defensive administration Decision-avoidance produced by treating goodfaith error as misconduct. Structured discretion Discretion that survives review because the criteria are published, the reasons recorded, the level fixed and an appeal provided. Disparate impact A facially neutral rule producing group-differentiated results; requires justification of the criterion, not proof of intent. Contestability The ability to appeal a decision, which presupposes being told the reason for it. Purpose limitation Data may be used only for the purpose for which it was collected; de-identification does not cure a change of purpose. Empathy fatigue Progressive blunting of responsiveness under repeated exposure to suffering; an occupational injury, not a defect of character. Emotional labour Hochschild — the unrecognised work of managing one’s own feeling as part of the job. Depersonalisation Maslach — treating the person as a case; the burnout symptom most damaging to service quality. Psychological safety Edmondson — whether a subordinate can report bad news without risk, which decides whether it arrives in time. Heckler’s veto Allowing a threat of disorder to determine whether a lawful right may be exercised. Entitlement failure Sen — deprivation arising from a collapse of access rather than an absence of supply. Exclusion and inclusion error Wrongly denying an eligible person against wrongly paying an ineligible one; the two are rarely symmetric in cost. Precautionary principle Where harm is irreversible and the exposed population vulnerable, absence of proof is not proof of absence. Public trust doctrine Office and public resources are held for others, on a fiduciary and not a contractual standard. Constitutional morality Ambedkar — the disposition to work institutions by their spirit; cultivated, not natural. Nudge Thaler and Sunstein — a change of choice architecture that must be cheap to avoid, which is the line between persuasion and manipulation. Decoupling Meyer and Rowan — the form adopted for legitimacy while the practice is unchanged.

Administrative vocabulary rather than governance vocabulary is the first thing that separates the copies. The terms carry the theory with them; an answer about ac- countability written without them reads as a General Studies answer and is marked
Zone of indifference Barnard — the band of orders obeyed without conscious question; widened by inducements.
Satisficing Simon — search stops at an acceptable rather than an optimal alternative.
Bounded rationality Simon — rationality limited by knowledge, computation and anticipation of one’s own preferences.
Decision premises Simon — authority operates by setting the premises of another’s decision, not by command.
Goal displacement Merton — the rule becomes an end in itself; means–ends inversion.
Trained incapacity Merton (after Veblen) — the very training that fits an officer for routine unfits him for the exception.
Co-optation Selznick — absorbing external elements into leadership to avert threats to stability; formal and informal.
Zones of uncertainty Crozier — power accumulates wherever a group controls the residual unpredictability.
Street-level discretion Lipsky — coping under scarcity by rationing, creaming, routinising and stereotyping.
Creaming Selecting the easiest cases so as to meet a target; a Lipsky coping mechanism.
Partisan mutual adjustment Lindblom — coordination achieved by many partisans adjusting to each other rather than by a centre.
Successive limited comparison Lindblom — comparing only marginally different alternatives against the status quo.
Formalism Riggs — the gap between prescribed norm and effective practice; measured by the compression ratio.
Heterogeneity Riggs — modern and traditional elements simultaneously present in one society.
Overlapping Riggs — formal structures penetrated by ascriptive social forces.
Sala Riggs — the administrative sub-system of the prismatic society.
Clect Riggs — a hybrid interest group, modern in form and ascriptive in membership.
Poly-normativism Riggs — competing and inconsistent normative standards operating together.
Soft State Myrdal — laws exist and non-compliance is tolerated.
Embedded autonomy Evans — corporate insulation plus dense ties to society; the developmental State’s condition.
Bureau-shaping Dunleavy — senior officials prefer small, elite, interesting policy work to large budgets.
Isomorphism DiMaggio & Powell — coercive, mimetic, normative pressures towards similarity of form.
Decoupling Meyer & Rowan — the form is adopted for legitimacy; the practice is not changed.
Equifinality Systems theory — the same end state reached by different routes; refutes the ‘one best way’.
Negative entropy Open systems import more energy than they expend and so resist decay.
Requisite variety Internal complexity must match environmental complexity.
Linking pin Likert — each supervisor belongs to two overlapping groups.
Law of the situation Follett — depersonalised orders; both parties obey what the situation requires.
Gangplank Fayol — sanctioned lateral communication across the scalar chain.
Clearance points Pressman & Wildavsky — each additional assent multiplies the probability of failure.
Authorising environment Moore — ministers, legislature, media and citizens whose authorisation a manager must secure.
Problem of many hands Bovens — where all are partly responsible, none is answerable.
Compression ratio Riggs — the measure of the gap between formal prescription and actual practice.
Iron law of oligarchy Michels — every organisation, however democratic, tends towards rule by a few.
Single- and double-loop learning Argyris & Schön — correcting the error vs questioning the governing value.
POSDCORB Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing, COordinating, Reporting, Budgeting (Gulick).
4 Ps of departmentalisation Purpose, Process, Persons (clientele), Place (Gulick).
Fayol’s five functions Planning, organising, commanding, coordinating, controlling.
Weber’s ideal type Rules and jurisdiction · hierarchy · files and written record · technical qualification · career with fixed salary · impersonality.
Barnard’s executive functions Maintain communication · secure essential services · formulate purpose.
Simon’s phases Intelligence · design · choice (review added later).
Maslow Physiological · safety · social · esteem · self-actualisation.
Alderfer ERG Existence · relatedness · growth, with frustration–regression.
Herzberg Hygiene: policy, supervision, salary, conditions, security. Motivators: achievement, recognition, work itself, responsibility, advancement.
Likert’s four systems 1 exploitative authoritative · 2 benevolent authoritative · 3 consultative · 4 participative group.
Blake & Mouton grid Concern for people × concern for production; 1,1 impoverished · 9,1 task · 1,9 country club · 5,5 middle-of-the-road · 9,9 team.
Hersey & Blanchard Telling · selling · participating · delegating, by follower readiness.
Riggs’s three societies Fused (agraria) · prismatic (transitia) · diffracted (industria).
Allison’s three models Rational actor · organisational process · bureaucratic politics.
Kingdon’s streams Problem · policy · politics, joined at a policy window.
Easton’s system Inputs (demands, support) · conversion · outputs · feedback.
Matland’s matrix Ambiguity × conflict: administrative · political · experimental · symbolic implementation.
Romzek & Dubnick Source of control (internal/external) × degree of control (high/low): hierarchical, legal, professional, political.

Presidential Reference opinion (20 Nov 2025) On Art 200/201: no judicially fixed timelines, no ‘deemed assent’; the assent function is not ordinarily justiciable before enactment, the exception being prolonged, unexplained and indefinite inaction — displacing the April 2025 Tamil Nadu judgment.
L. Chandra Kumar (1997) High Court review under Arts 226/227 is a basic feature; tribunals are supplementary, not substitutional.
S. P. Sampath Kumar (1987) Exclusion of High Court jurisdiction upheld on condition of a real alternative — reversed above.
R. Gandhi (2010) · Rojer Mathew (2019) · Madras Bar Association (2021) Successive tribunal appointment and tenure rules struck down for want of independence.
In re Delhi Laws Act (1951) Delegated legislation permissible; the essential legislative function may not be delegated.
Tulsiram Patel (1985) Art 311(2) exceptions upheld; limited review of the recorded satisfaction.
Dev Dutt (2008) Every entry in the appraisal, including ‘good’, must be communicated — the origin of full PAR disclosure.
T. K. Rangarajan (2003) No fundamental, statutory or moral right of government employees to strike.
T. S. R. Subramanian (2013) Civil Services Board, minimum tenure, and oral instructions to be reduced to writing.
Prakash Singh (2006) Seven directions on police reform — SSC, DGP selection and tenure, fixed tenure, separation of investigation, Establishment Board, Complaints Authority, NSC.
Vineet Narain (1997) CVC’s supervisory role over the CBI; insulation of investigation; the ‘single directive’ struck down.
Lalita Kumari (2013) FIR registration mandatory for a cognisable offence.
D. K. Basu (1997) · Arnesh Kumar (2014) Arrest and custody safeguards; notice of appearance instead of arrest.
Maneka Gandhi (1978) Procedure must be fair, just and reasonable — the foundation of Indian administrative due process.
E. P. Royappa (1974) Arbitrariness is itself a denial of equality under Art 14.
Puttaswamy (2017) Informational privacy; the four-part proportionality test now applied to administrative action.
Ajay Hasia / R. D. Shetty The tests for ‘other authorities’ under Art 12 — why a PSU carries writ liability its competitor does not.
ADR (2002) · PUCL (2003) · Lily Thomas (2013) Voter’s right to know; candidate affidavits; end of the s. 8(4) appeal-pending protection.
Mohit Minerals (2022) GST Council recommendations are persuasive, not binding on either legislature.
Vishaka (1997) Judicially framed administrative guidelines pending legislation — later the POSH Act 2013.
Paper I theory carried across — the concept and the Paper II use

Weber — legal-rational, patrimonial, prebendal Kautilya and the Mughals as patrimonial/prebendal; Art 311 as the condition for impersonality; ‘rule of officials’ as the risk in the political–permanent executive question.

Riggs — formalism, overlapping, sala, clect The single most useful import: every ‘body exists, government does not’ finding — PESA, DPC, Ward Committees, State Security Commissions. Compression ratio for the gap.
Meyer & Rowan — decoupling Prakash Singh compliance; JNNURM reform conditionality; regulator independence in form.
DiMaggio & Powell — isomorphism Why the form is adopted at all: coercive (judicial direction, grant condition), mimetic (Smart City SPVs), normative (NPM vocabulary).
Merton — goal displacement, trained incapacity Utilisation certificate as the target; file movement as work; the officer trained for the exception.
Selznick — co-optation, institutionalisation Community Development and every participatory programme since; Indianisation changing composition and not character.

Simon — bounded rationality, satisficing, decision premises Unranked PSU objectives; the file as the organisation’s store of premises; why an analytical unit beats a differently-recruited Joint Secretary.
Lipsky — street-level discretion Targeting failure at the counter; FIR refusal as rationing; suppressed demand under MGNREGA.
Pressman & Wildavsky — clearance points Centrally sponsored schemes; the elected/appointed district duality; multi-agency city government.
Matland — ambiguity × conflict Why better design will not rescue land, forest and environmental programmes: symbolic implementation.
Elmore — backward mapping MGNREGA’s design; Aspirational Districts; the general prescription for Indian implementation failure.
Wildavsky — base and increment Parliamentary financial control; why the guillotine matters; why ZBB and PPBS failed.
Goodhart MoU composite scores clustering at the top; PAR gradings without variance; utilisation certificates; index-based competitive federalism.
Dunleavy — bureau-shaping Preference for missions and societies over departments; retention of enterprise portfolios; NPM-is-dead and digital-era governance for the India Stack.
Hood — the seven NPM doctrines Disaggregation in parastatals and SPVs; competition in Swachh Survekshan; output controls in the Outcome Budget.
Osborne & Gaebler · Denhardt Steering not rowing — arriving without steering capacity; the New Public Service as the corrective.
Evans — embedded autonomy The developmental-state defence of retaining productive presence; space, atomic energy and telecom as Indian counter-cases to the licence-permit period.
Ostrom — design principles, nesting, polycentricity PESA and the Gram Sabha; why the DPC fails the nesting condition; why the fragmented city is not automatically inefficient.

Romzek & Dubnick Hierarchical, legal, professional, political — use to show that Indian reform multiplies legal accountability where professional accountability has no institutional home. Finer vs Friedrich External enforceable control vs inner responsibility — the frame for neutrality, for the PSU board, and for regulators. Bovens — problem of many hands PMO/Cabinet Committee traceability; multi-agency city failure. Myrdal — soft State Criminalisation, enforcement gaps, the anti-corruption chain. Klitgaard Monopoly + discretion – accountability: the reason preventive egovernance has out-performed the punitive chain. Hirschman — exit, voice, loyalty RTI, service guarantees, social audit as institutions of voice where exit is unavailable. Sassen · Harvey Global city; managerialism to entrepreneurialism — the global–local question. Kingdon — policy window Why RTI passed and police reform did not. Heeks — design–reality gap Public IT project failure; process transplantation in e-governance. Numbers, ratios and dates worth carrying Enterprise forms Government company: not less than 51% government holding; CAG audit under s. 143(5). MoU system from 1987–88; Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna as graded delegation; disinvestment phases 1991–92, 1999, ETFs, 2021 policy. Fiscal Sixteenth FC devolution 41% of the divisible pool, award period 2026– 31. FRBM Review debt anchor 60% general government (40 Union, 20 States). States: roughly 60% of general government expenditure, about a third of revenue. Municipal own revenue around 1% of GDP. Local government Panchayats: three tiers above 20 lakh population; onethird reservation for women (many States 50%); five-year term, election within six months of dissolution; Eleventh Schedule 29 matters; Twelfth Schedule 18; Ward Committees above 3 lakh; MPC above 10 lakh; DPC fourfifths elected, MPC two-thirds. Committees of Parliament PAC 22 · Estimates 30 (Lok Sabha only) · COPU 22 · 24 Departmentally Related Standing Committees of 21 each, since 1993. Rights and timelines RTI 30 days, 48 hours for life and liberty, first appeal 30 days, penalty up to ₹25,000. MGNREGA 100 days, work within 15 days else unemployment allowance, 60:40 wage–material, social audit every six months. NHRC: custodial death or rape intimated within 24 hours; complaint limitation one year; term three years after the 2019 amendment. Personnel Cabinet Secretary tenure two years, extendable to four. Second ARC’s intensive reviews at 14 and 20 years. Prakash Singh minimum tenure two years for DGP and field officers. Unified Pension Scheme from 1 April 2025 — 50% of the average of the last twelve months’ basic pay after 25 years of qualifying service.
